newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Thai PM in Manila for trade talks and golf.
newsitem.headline: Thai PM in Manila for trade talks and golf.

text.p: Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh arrived in Manila on Wednesday on a two-day visit that has raised speculation of a possible rice deal with the Philippines.
Chavalit will have two meetings and play a round of golf with President Fidel Ramos during his visit and speak at the prestigious Makati Business Club on Thursday.
Trade sources in Bangkok said last week they expected Chavalit to conclude a rice deal during his Manila visit. There was no official confirmation in Manila of the deal.

Thailand ranked as the Philippines' 10th-biggest trading partner in 1995, according to available official figures, and was one of the sources of rice imports when Manila was hit by serious shortage in 1995.

Chavalit's visit coincides with a controversy over a Manila Bay reclamation project which involves the Amari Coastal Bay Development Corp, in which one of Thailand's largest construction contractors, Italian Thai Development Plc, is a shareholder.

Philippine Senate President Ernesto Macada had questioned the deal, saying the contract to develop the area was grossly undervalued. Both Amari and Manila's Public Estates Authority, which entered into contracts with different property firms to develop the area, have denied any wrong-doing.
Ramos last month ordered that the contracts be reviewed.
Foreign Secretary Domingo Siazon said last week the reclamation deal was "an internal affair" of the Philippines and he did not expect it to come up in the Ramos-Chavalit talks.
